nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate parses natural-language policy changes into inspectable executable predicates rather than only presenting metrics.
Candidate produces a one-page consequence brief with affected groups, uncertainty, and human-review cases.

nearest_analogues.name: Generic chatbot wrapper over a sponsor API
differences: Candidate requires the AI output to become executable simulation predicates with cited source fields.
No sponsor API wrapper is central; the demo runs on synthetic civic records and rule edits.

nearest_analogues.name: 3nd03/commitment-ledger
differences: Commitment-ledger tracks parliamentary commitments in Hansard and written answers; candidate simulates consequences of proposed rules on synthetic civic-service data.
Candidate's observable demo is before/after counterfactual impact, not follow-up tracking.

observable_differentiator: Live natural-language rule edit becomes inspectable predicates, before/after segment deltas, uncertainty bands, and an MP-readable consequence brief.
notes: Nearest provided matches are generic crowded archetypes or a parliamentary-adjacent GitHub project with a different data source and workflow. No decisive analogue shares user, problem, mechanism, data, action, and demo.

nearest_analogues.name: Document / PDF summariser
differences: Candidate verifies a correction against evidence and emits a structured patch, not just a summary.
Candidate writes a signed append-only correction event and changes workflow state after human confirmation.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate performs a workflow-state-changing correction rather than a read-only dashboard.
Correction receipt includes before/after value, evidence hashes, rationale, timestamp, and reviewer confirmation.

nearest_analogues.name: 3nd03/commitment-ledger
differences: Both use ledger-like provenance in a parliamentary context, but commitment-ledger tracks public commitments while candidate handles resident casework corrections.
Candidate's demo applies or blocks a correction request against fictional evidence, not commitment follow-up discovery.

observable_differentiator: A proposed casework correction is AI-checked against evidence, converted into a human-confirmed structured patch, applied to the queue, and recorded as a tamper-evident receipt.
notes: The provenance-ledger motif is familiar, but the workflow-level correction action and evidence-backed before/after receipt create a materially different demo from the nearest analogues.

nearest_analogues.name: Meeting notes / productivity chatbot
differences: Candidate claims constraint simulation over roles, dependencies, deadlines, and calendar capacity rather than drafting generic follow-up notes.
Output includes a bounded evidence-review task with stop condition and rationale for rejected alternatives.

nearest_analogues.name: Recommendation list with no last-mile action
differences: Candidate writes a calendar-ready task instead of stopping at recommendations.
Demo must show an editable claim or deadline changing the scheduled next action.

nearest_analogues.name: 3nd03/commitment-ledger
differences: Commitment-ledger tracks whether parliamentary commitments were followed up; candidate schedules the next bounded review action after a pitch.
Candidate uses synthetic constraints and calendars, not Hansard or written answers.

observable_differentiator: The demo must visibly solve a constrained scheduling problem by selecting one feasible, uncertainty-reducing next action and exporting it as a calendar-ready task.
notes: This is close to crowded meeting-notes and follow-up-assistant territory. It survives only if the demo clearly shows constraint-based selection, rejected alternatives, stop conditions, and calendar-ready action rather than generic AI task drafting.

nearest_analogues.name: Dashboard-only analytics without an irreversible state change
differences: Candidate anchors raw evidence snapshots with hashes and keeps hash references stable after model feedback.
Candidate produces an audit-ready alert bundle rather than only visual anomaly cards.

nearest_analogues.name: Carbon-footprint tracker dashboard
differences: Candidate focuses on procurement or grant-event anomalies rather than emissions tracking.
Evidence anchoring and alert rationale are core demo elements, not just trend visualization.

nearest_analogues.name: 3nd03/commitment-ledger
differences: Commitment-ledger tracks parliamentary statements and follow-up; candidate scores procurement/grant events for anomalies.
Candidate's demo centers on split-invoice or supplier-pattern detection with immutable record hashes.

observable_differentiator: Clicking an anomaly exposes implicated records, feature-level rationale, and immutable hash receipts that remain unchanged after feedback updates future labels.
notes: Anomaly dashboards are crowded, and procurement fraud analytics is a known category. The cryptographic evidence anchoring is a substantive differentiator only if it is visible in the demo and tied to feedback/model-change behavior.
